edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: These exposures are thought to build cognitive reserve by repeatedly engaging distributed language, memory, and executive networks over time. For Dementia (all-cause), reserve does not necessarily prevent pathology but can delay the point at which underlying disease becomes clinically visible.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link cognitive engagement to lower risk of dementia (all-cause) in older adults. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
